facts.text: From Tokyo, the easiest and most popular option is a direct bus from Shinjuku to the trailhead at Kawaguchiko Fifth Station.
facts.quote: direct bus from  Shinjuku to the trailhead at Kawaguchiko Fifth Station

facts.text: The Keio/Fujikyu Express Bus runs from Shinjuku Expressway Bus Terminal to Lake Kawaguchi; separate buses go to Kawaguchiko 5th station and do not run if snow blocks the route.
facts.quote: does not run if snow blocks the route

facts.text: During warm months, buses run from Shinjuku directly to the 5th station.
facts.quote: buses run from Shinjuku directly to the 5th station

facts.text: Once on the mountain, the only way of getting around is on foot.
facts.quote: the only way of getting around is on foot

facts.text: Horseback riding is available on the Fujiguchiko trail between the 5th and 7th stations only, for ¥14,000.
facts.quote: horseback riding, available on the Fujiguchiko trail between the 5th and 7th stations only

facts.text: Official climbing season lasts from early July to early September, with exact dates varying by year and trail.
facts.quote: from early July to early September

facts.text: Even during climbing season, temperatures at the top can be below freezing at night, so climbers must dress adequately.
facts.quote: temperatures at the top can be below freezing at night

facts.text: Climbing outside the official season is extremely dangerous without alpine climbing experience and equipment; nearly all facilities are closed and all roads to the 5th station are shut out of season.
facts.quote: All roads to the 5th station are shut out of season

facts.text: Outside the official season, climbers are required to submit a climbing plan to the Yamanashi Prefectural Police or Shizuoka Prefectural Police; this has been mandatory since 2019.
facts.quote: required to submit a climbing plan to the Yamanashi Prefectural Police or Shizuoka Prefectural Police

facts.text: Buses from Shinjuku to Lake Kawaguchi cost ¥1750; separate buses to Kawaguchiko 5th station cost ¥1540 one way or ¥2100 round trip.
Tolls from inner Tokyo via the Chuo Expressway from Shinjuku are around ¥2500.
facts.quote: Tolls will set you back around ¥2500

facts.text: Climbing outside the official season is extremely dangerous without alpine climbing experience and equipment; winter weather is vicious and people have been blown off the mountain by high winds.
